title: n8n
summary: A workflow automation platform with cloud and self-hosting paths and execution-based cloud pricing.

sources.title: Which license do I need for my use case?
Deploy with the AI starter kit

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: Connects applications and APIs in customizable, low-code workflows; supports custom nodes and AI functionality.

facts.label: Deployment
facts.value: Official docs describe n8n Cloud and self-hosted installation options such as npm and Docker. n8n's security guidance says operators must configure TLS termination and handle encryption at rest.

facts.label: License model
facts.value: n8n's repository license applies its Sustainable Use License to covered code and permits use or modification for the user's own internal business purposes or non-commercial/personal use; source files with .ee. in the filename or directory are excluded and require an applicable Enterprise license. n8n's support guidance says hosting and managing clients' workflows and credentials on your own instance requires Enterprise, while embedding n8n to expose workflows to customers requires a white-labeled Embed license. Consulting on a client's own internal instance does not itself require a commercial license for the consultant. These vendor examples do not determine a specific deployment's terms; confirm the exact use case and entitlements with n8n.

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: n8n's Privacy Policy says it processes certain Usage Data for self-hosted deployments unless users opt out, including user identifiers, account settings, user events, workflow usage metrics and enabled integrations. It says users can object with future effect; an email address may be submitted for usage-related contact. This does not verify a specific instance's setting or data handled by connected services.

facts.label: Local model inference
facts.value: n8n documents a built-in Ollama Chat Model and Ollama credentials; the documented Base URL defaults to a local Ollama endpoint (`http://localhost:11434`) and can also target remote authenticated Ollama instances. Its self-hosted AI Starter Kit combines self-hosted n8n with Ollama for local LLMs, but n8n describes the kit as a proof-of-concept/demo and says to harden it before production. When n8n and Ollama run in separate containers, network configuration may be required. This is a documented integration path, not evidence about a specific deployment's inference location, data flow or production suitability. No model or instance was tested.

facts.label: Workflow portability
facts.value: n8n documents workflow JSON download/import, Server CLI exports, API endpoints and n8n CLI packages for moving workflows. It recommends its CLI for new command-line moves; packages carry workflow folders, projects and references but remain in Preview. CLI `--backup` exports workflows and credentials only, not users/roles, execution history/logs, variables or instance settings (including the encryption key). Full instance recovery can also require the `.n8n` folder, database, external binary/execution storage and custom nodes. Workflow JSON may expose credential names/IDs and cURL-imported auth headers; protect and sanitize it before sharing. No cross-instance migration or restore was tested.

prices.name: Starter (n8n Cloud)
prices.billing: Displayed monthly equivalent, billed annually; confirm applicable region and taxes at checkout.
prices.allowance: 2,500 workflow executions per month with unlimited steps.

sections.heading: Estimate complete workflow runs
paragraphs: The Cloud pricing page counts a workflow execution as one run regardless of the number of steps. Estimate schedule and event frequency first, then test retries and failure behavior with representative data.

sections.heading: Compare hosting responsibility
paragraphs: Cloud pricing and self-hosted deployment move different operating responsibilities to the buyer. Before choosing self-hosting, account for upgrades, backups, secrets, monitoring and the license terms that apply to the planned use.

sections.heading: Separate workflow export from instance recovery
paragraphs: Official docs describe workflow JSON import/export and an n8n CLI package path that remains in Preview. CLI backup exports workflows and credentials, not a complete instance; full recovery may also need the user folder and encryption key, database, external storage and custom nodes. Review exported JSON for credential names or authentication headers, and test the selected move/restore path before relying on it.

sections.heading: Connect to an Ollama model endpoint
paragraphs: n8n documents an Ollama Chat Model integration and an AI Starter Kit that pairs self-hosted n8n with Ollama for local LLMs. Its credentials default to a local Ollama URL, but can also point to remote authenticated instances. Separate containers may need explicit network configuration, and n8n says the starter kit is for proof-of-concept/demo use and needs production hardening.

pros.text: n8n documents low-code connections between apps and APIs, with custom nodes available for extending workflows.
The documentation presents both n8n Cloud and self-hosted installation paths, including npm and Docker.
n8n documents an Ollama Chat Model integration and a self-hosted starter kit that pairs n8n with Ollama for local LLMs.

cons.text: Self-hosting requires an operator to own deployment and ongoing instance responsibilities; no deployment test was performed for this profile.

n8n's Sustainable Use License limits use to internal business or non-commercial/personal purposes; its support guidance identifies separate commercial licenses for hosting client workflows or embedding n8n for customers.

A local Ollama endpoint needs to be reachable from n8n; different containers may need network configuration, and n8n says its starter kit is for proof-of-concept/demo use rather than production-ready deployment. No setup was tested.

faqs.question: Can n8n be self-hosted?
faqs.answer: Yes. Official docs list cloud and self-hosted options, including npm and Docker. Review the current license and plan terms before adopting it for a business use case.

faqs.question: What should I budget for n8n Cloud?
faqs.answer: Use the current plan page and confirm regional checkout terms; this draft's displayed amount is not a checkout quote.

faqs.question: Can a consultant host clients' workflows in their own n8n instance?
faqs.answer: n8n's support guidance says hosting and managing clients' workflows and credentials in your own instance requires an Enterprise license. Embedding n8n to expose workflows to customers requires a white-labeled Embed license. Consulting on a client's own internal instance does not itself require a commercial license for the consultant, while the client's needs depend on its use case. Confirm the exact model with n8n; this summary is vendor guidance, not a legal determination.

faqs.question: Can a workflow export move a complete n8n instance?
faqs.answer: No. n8n supports workflow JSON download/import and an n8n CLI package path that carries workflow folders, projects and references, but packages are in Preview. Its CLI backup covers workflows and credentials only, not users/roles, execution history/logs, variables or instance settings including the encryption key. Full restore may also require the `.n8n` folder, database, external storage and custom nodes. Workflow JSON can expose credential names/IDs or authentication headers; protect and sanitize exports. No cross-instance move was tested.

faqs.question: Can n8n use a locally run model?
faqs.answer: n8n documents a built-in Ollama Chat Model and an AI Starter Kit that combines self-hosted n8n with Ollama for local LLMs. The Ollama credential defaults to `http://localhost:11434` but can also target a remote authenticated instance; separate containers may require network configuration. n8n describes the starter kit as a proof-of-concept/demo and says to harden it before production. This does not verify any deployment's data flow or model setup; no inference was tested.

verdict: Evaluate n8n when workflows need API-level flexibility or self-hosting is a requirement. Compare execution volume and operating ownership rather than counting workflow steps alone.
bestFor: Builders connecting APIs and applications who can estimate full workflow executions
notFor: Teams that have not checked the fair-code terms or cannot own the chosen hosting path
migration: Export representative workflows and credentials separately. Test node availability, error handling, schedules and secrets in a non-production instance before cutover.
gaps: Confirm the exact deployment and feature entitlements against the current license and plan; public vendor guidance distinguishes internal use from hosting client workflows or embedding, but no specific use case, agreement or entitlement was reviewed. Confirm regional checkout price before a business recommendation.
Self-hosting shifts infrastructure and security operations to the operator; no deployment test was performed for this profile.
Verify the selected instance's telemetry opt-out, connected-service and model-provider data terms, and actual TLS/at-rest encryption configuration; no account or deployment was inspected.
Verify that the selected n8n instance can reach its Ollama endpoint, the intended model behaves as required, and workflow data follows the required path; no instance, network or model was tested.

The documented workflow JSON, CLI package and CLI backup methods have different scopes; confirm the exact projects, users, execution data, variables, secrets, instance settings, external storage and custom-node requirements for a move. No cross-instance migration or restore was tested.
